jobs.description: Frequently Asked Questions - Tangos Skip to main content # Frequently Asked Questions # Questions about Tangos ### What Tangos Is 01 What is Tangos? + × Tangos is an autonomous investigation model for risk and compliance. It runs an investigation from start to finish: forming a hypothesis, gathering evidence across jurisdictions and languages, recording every reasoning step, and delivering a case file built to the standard an examiner expects. Your team reviews the finished case instead of assembling it. 02 How is this different from the detection tools we already run? + × Detection tools decide what to flag. Tangos handles what happens after the flag. Alert volumes, screening coverage, and transaction monitoring have all improved over the past decade. The investigation of each escalated case is still done by hand, and that is the work Tangos takes on. 03 Is Tangos a copilot for our analysts? + × No. A copilot waits for a prompt and hands back a draft. Tangos runs the investigation itself and produces a finished case file with the evidence and reasoning attached. Your investigators come in at review and sign-off, not at data collection. 04 What does a finished case file contain? + × A conclusion, the evidence behind it, and the reasoning that connects the two. Every claim is anchored to a specific source, so a reviewer can follow any finding back to where it came from. Each case carries an immutable audit trail of how it was worked. --- ### Defensibility 05 Will an examiner accept a case Tangos produced? + × No vendor can promise you an examiner's verdict. What you can control is whether the work survives examination, and that comes down to whether a reviewer can reconstruct the decision. Cases are built against supervisory expectations, including those set by FinCEN and the FCA, and every conclusion carries its source attribution and reasoning trail. 06 How do we know the conclusions are not invented? + × Every claim in a case is tied to a specific source. Nothing enters a report without a traceable origin, and the reasoning that produced each finding is recorded rather than summarized after the fact. A finding that cannot be sourced does not enter the case file. 07 What happens when Tangos gets something wrong? + × You see it, because the reasoning is visible. A wrong turn shows up as a traceable step your reviewer can inspect and reject, not as an unexplained output. Review sits at the decisions that carry consequence, which is where your investigators apply judgment. The errors worth fearing are the ones nobody can examine. Keeping reasoning inspectable is how this design addresses them. --- ### Accountability And Your People 08 Who is accountable for the decision? + × Your institution. Tangos builds the case and documents how it was built. The filing decision, the escalation, and the sign-off stay with your people. Accountability does not transfer to a vendor, and any system that implies otherwise is worth questioning. 09 Does Tangos replace our investigators? + × It changes what they spend the day doing. Investigators shift from data collection to judgment. They review, challenge, and apply institutional knowledge no system can replicate. The capacity gain shows up as more cases resolved at the same headcount, not as a smaller team. ## Ready to transform your investigation workflow? Tangos works alongside your existing stack and does not require production access to your systems. A proof of value runs on historical cases your team has already closed, so no integration project stands between you and a result you can judge. ### Deployment And Getting Started 11 Can Tangos run inside our own environment? + × Yes, three ways.
